segments.text: Good evening. This is Aakash Mani. I am Anuja Kumar with the news at 9.
The headlines. Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurates
Bharat Parv 2026 at Ekta Nagar in Gujarat marking the beginning of 151st
birth anniversary celebrations of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
The extreme poverty in the country declined from 27.1% in 2011 to 2.6% in 2023, says World
Bank's poverty and equity brief.
In West Bengal, over 7,000 people evacuated to safer locations as water level of Sankosh
River in Alipur Dwar district rises due to glacial lake outburst flood in Bhutan.
6 people died in a helicopter crash at Hathi Parvath Hills of Chamoli district in Uttarakhand.
Government announces nationwide census from 25th January to 28th February next year, excluding
snow and polebound states.
And Manisha Bhanwala becomes first Indian woman to win a gold medal at wrestling world
championships in Kazakhstan.
And now the news in detail.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated Bharat Parvot 2026 at Ekthanagar in Gujarat's
Narmada district today, ahead of the rastriya Ekthadevas celebrations.
Tomorrow, on the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabh Bhai Patel, the Prime Minister
will pay floral tributes at the Statue of Unity and dedicate multiple development projects
to the nation.
More from our correspondent.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated Bharat Parva, cultural festival reflecting spirit
of Aik Bharat Thrist Bharat that will continue till November 15.
The Prime Minister is also scheduled to witness the Ekta Prakash Parva, an illumination festival
featuring 530 meter illuminated stretch and 180 meter glow tunnel, tomorrow marking
151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patil.
Prime Minister will inaugurate and lay foundation stone for 31 tourism and infrastructure projects
over 426 crore rupees.
This includes IRCTC Hotel, Ekta Cruise, Rainforest Project.
In the evening, the Prime Minister will participate in the Rastya Ekta Diwali celebrations,
which will feature the Ekta Parade by Security Forces.
Chirag Guranya, Akashwani News, Ahmedabad.
Prime Minister Modi began his two-day Gujarat visit from Banaskar to this morning.
He launched development projects worth more than 14,000 crore rupees, including state-of-the-art
Bharat-Bhavain Breeding and Research Centre and Banas Bio-CNG plants in Radhanpur and
Tarard.
Upon reaching Banas Khattah this morning, the Prime Minister held a roadshow and was
accorded a grand welcome.
The Prime Minister also released the 24th installment under PM Kisan, amounting to
nearly 19,000 crore rupees.

The World Bank's poverty and equity report this month
has highlighted country's progress
as one of the fastest poverty declines in the world.
In a social media post,
Finance Minister Nirmala Sitaraman said that over 49
crore people have moved above the lower middle income
poverty line during the same period.
She mentioned that employment in India also increased
by 13.4 crore people between 2017 and 2023, nearly twice the increase in the working age
population.
Ms. Sita Raman said, the government's sustained policy efforts are yielding tangible results,
strengthening the foundations for inclusive growth and greater economic opportunity.
Government today announced that population census will be conducted across the country
except in snowbound and polebound states from 25th of January to 28th of February next year.
Home Ministry issued a notification declaring the census of population in all states and union territories
except Manipur, Goa, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Uttarakhand, Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir.
A revision round will be held from the 1st to 5th of March, 2027.
There shall be an option for self-enumeration from 10th of January to 24th of January for
the conduct of the census.
Telecom regulatory authority of India Try today released draft guidelines on responsible use
of artificial intelligence in telecommunication networks and provision of telecommunication

The draft has been placed on Try's website.
This is Aakashwani giving you the news.
Welcome back to the evening news on Aakashwani.
Home Minister Amit Shah today said the BJP would implement the Uniform Civil Code UCC
see in Uttar Pradesh expressing confidence that the party would return to power in the
state after assembly elections next year.
Addressing the BJP State Working Committee meeting in Lucknow today, he urged the party
workers to work with full commitment to secure another victory with a clear majority.
He credited party workers for the BJP's victories in the 2017 and 2022 assembly elections.
The BJP government in Tappurdees is as firm as like Angad's foot.
It is impossible to dislodge.
The Bharti Janta Party is set to form the government here for the third consecutive
time and party workers need not have any apprehensions.
In 2022, we secured 41 percent of votes well above the majority mark and returned to
power for the second consecutive term.
A helicopter travelling from Badrinath Dham to the Sahastraddhara helipad in Dehradun crashed
in the Hathi Parvath Hills above Chai village in the Joshi Math area of Chamoli district
this afternoon.
All six people on board, including the pilot, died in the accident.
According to Secretary of Disaster Management and Rehabilitation, information about the
crash was received at around 2 p.m.
All the passengers on board were from Karnataka.
Governor Dr. Dhal Singh Bisain and Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami expressed deep grief over
the loss of lives and conveyed their condolences to the bereaved families.
Chief Minister Dhami has also directed a detailed investigation into the cause of
the accident.
In West Bengal, around 7,000 people living along the Sankosh River in Alipurdwa district
have been shifted to safer locations following a rise in the river's water level caused by
a glacial lake outburst flood in Bhutan.
The Sankosh River has risen by nearly two feet since morning.
The river flows along the interstate boundary between West Bengal and Assam, more from our
correspondent.
The precautionary evacuation was carried out on Thursday night following reports of
a glacial lake bridge in Bhutan which raised fears of possible flooding in areas
along the Sankosh River.
More than 7,000 people were evacuated and accommodated in 18 relief camps.
Several residents from neighboring Assam also took shelter in relief camps in Kumar Gram
near the Assam border in Aliput district.
Although the river water level rose slightly on Friday afternoon, officials said it was
still below the danger mark and had not reached an alarming level.
The administration continues to closely monitor the situation to ensure the safety
of people living in vulnerable areas.
The aftermath of Cyclone Ornob has left devastation trail in large parts of southern Orisha.
Ganjam, Gajapati and Kandamal are among the worst affected districts, although floodwaters
are receding. Several villages remained marooned, and the suffering of affected people continues
to mount. Landslides, damaged roads and disrupted rail services have compounded the crisis,
officers, even as rescue and relief operations are being intensified, more from our correspondent.
Chief Minister Mohan Charan Maaji has conducted an aerial survey of the flood hit districts
and directed officials to expedite relief operations.
President Draupadi Murmaud, today spoke to Chief Minister Mr. Maaji and was apprised
of the flood situation in Odisha.
Meanwhile, 30 additional officers have been deployed in Ganjam.
The Coast Guard, NDRF and ODRAF are engaged in rescuing stranded people with helicopter
support.
train services have also been severely disrupted with several cancellations. In Kandamal,
three members of a family, including a nine-month-old infant, were killed when a landslide buried
their house under mud and debris in Dangi's village. Landslides have also damaged roads
and paralyzed normal life. Meanwhile, the rising Jalaka River has triggered fresh flood
concerns in low-lying areas of northern Odisha. Prakash Das for Akaswani News, Bhubaneswar.
A low-pressure area remnant of Cyclone Ornab over North Chattisgarh and adjoining East Madhya
Pradesh persisted over the region today.
Meanwhile, another low-pressure area over South Andaman Sea and adjoining Andaman Nicobar
Island persisted over the region.
The Indian Space Research Organization, ISRO, will launch the NBS-03 navigation satellite
from the Satish Dhawan Space Center in Sri Haricota tonight.
GSLV-F-18 rocket in its milestone 20th flight will carry the satellite at 11.51pm.
It aims to boost India's independent NAVIC system by deploying an advanced satellite
equipped with an indigenous atomic clock.
Indian Railways has geared up to manage the ongoing festive season rush
with extensive crowd management preparations underway at several railway stations.
Ministry of Railways said that Indian Railways is developing
The holding areas have been designed to accommodate passengers before they proceed to the platform
area.
Urna Railway Station in Gujarat is an important example of a station having the modern passenger
passenger-holding area is especially beneficial for migrant passengers travelling to their
hometowns across different parts of the country during the festive season.
The facility has been equipped with 10 ticket counters, 120 seats, 55 CCTV cameras, 6 electronic
train display boards, a public announcement system and Wi-Fi connectivity.
The aim is to reduce congestion on platforms in circulating areas and at station approaches
by providing designated spaces for waiting and ticketing.
on to sports. Manisha Bhanwala scripted history by becoming the first Indian woman to win a gold medal
at the wrestling world championships in Astana, Kazakhstan. She also became only the second Indian
wrestler to claim a world championship title after Sushil Kumar, who won the men's 66 kg gold
in 2010. Manisha clenched the women's 59 kg gold with a remarkable eight-six comeback victory
over American wrestler Abigail Nette in the final.
In men's cricket, Horst New Zealand defeated India by 87 runs in the 4th G20 international
at Eden Park in Auckland.
Chasing a massive target of 260 runs, India managed to score 172 for 9 in their allotted
20 overs.
Earlier put into bat first, New Zealand posted a massive 259 for 7, powered by a spectacular
century by Glenn Phillips, scoring 107 runs off 49 balls.
Prasad Bharati has brought laurels to India with Nongmai Thaim Nandakumar Singh
winning the prestigious ABU Broadcast Engineering Excellence Award
in 2026 for his outstanding contribution to broadcast technology and innovation.
And now before we end the bulletin, the headlines once again.

marking the beginning of 151st birth anniversary celebrations of Sardar Vallabhaya Patel. Extreme

poverty and equity brief. In West Bengal, over 7,000 people evacuated to safer locations
as water level of Sankoshtra Varena Lipur Dua district rises due to glacial lake outburst
flood in Bhutan and Manisha Bhanwala becomes the first Indian woman to win gold medal at
wrestling world championships in Kazakhstan.
